explanation: Exchanging business cards is considered polite and normal in US business settings, and etiquette is notably relaxed compared with Europe or Asia. Cards are commonly offered at the start of a meeting or during networking to share names and roles, though you should not force cards on uninterested people or hand them out indiscriminately.
local_tip: Offer your card naturally during conversation or at the start of a meeting, and skip it outside work contexts where it can seem tacky.

also_check.note: Card exchange is a formal, ritualized two-handed gesture with a bow and careful reading of the card.
Cards are typically presented and received with both hands, often with the text facing the recipient.
Exchange is common but more formal and reserved than in the US, usually at the start of a meeting.
